study.title: Spontaneous Hyperinflation of Intragastric Balloon Presenting as Acute Pancreatitis

cover.headline: A weight-loss balloon **inflated on its own inside a patient** and triggered acute pancreatitis.

slides.title: Doctors placed an intragastric balloon for obesity management, then documented what happened when it hyperinflated.
slides.body:
An intragastric balloon is a temporary implant used to help manage obesity. It sits in the stomach and is normally filled with a fixed volume of fluid. This case tracked one patient whose balloon spontaneously overinflated weeks after placement.

The team used endoscopy to assess the balloon, found it had grown far larger than intended, and linked the expansion to Candida fungal infection inside the device. The inflated balloon was compressing nearby organs.

slides.title: The hyperinflated balloon was associated with pancreatic compression, and the patient developed acute pancreatitis.
slides.body:
Imaging showed the balloon had expanded enough to compress the pancreas from outside. The patient presented with symptoms of acute pancreatitis, a painful inflammatory condition. Lab work and scans confirmed the diagnosis.

Doctors removed the balloon urgently via endoscopy. After removal, the pancreatitis resolved completely and the patient's symptoms disappeared. The fungal overgrowth inside the balloon appeared to generate gas, driving the hyperinflation.

caveats: This is a single case report, not a controlled trial comparing outcomes across many patients.
The study found a pattern, not a cause. Something else could explain the link between balloon hyperinflation and pancreatitis.

cta.headline: Send this to anyone considering an intragastric balloon
cta.sub: One real study, every weekday. The full paper is linked in bio.

caption: Intragastric balloons are reversible devices placed in the stomach to help manage obesity, but this case shows a rare complication. One patient's balloon hyperinflated due to Candida fungal infection inside the device, expanding enough to compress the pancreas and trigger acute pancreatitis. Endoscopic removal led to complete resolution. The report appeared in DEN open and involved a single patient tracked after balloon placement. This is a case report, so it documents one unusual event rather than testing a treatment across a group. Full study: doi.org/10.1002/deo2.70414 — Send this to anyone weighing the risks of weight-loss devices before making a decision.
